Paragraph: In Bhagavad Gita Chapter 3, Verse 21, Krishna instructs Arjuna: 'Whatever action a great leader performs, common people follow. Whatever standards they set by exemplary acts, all the world pursues. Therefore, act responsibly for the benefit of society.'
Situation/Problem_Faced: Desire to withdraw from social obligations, burnout, and lack of purpose.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna emphasizes societal responsibility (Lokasangraha), urging Arjuna to lead by ethical example.
Outcome/Resolution: Finding meaning in social responsibility helps overcome personal apathy and isolation.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Lokasangraha (Action performed for the welfare and cohesion of the world)
Svadharma (Personal duty within the social framework)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Individual action must serve global harmony; true leaders act selflessly to set high ethical standards for all.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Highlights social role model dynamics, value-driven living, and overcoming existential purposelessness.
